start.text: Plot twist—this one actually isn't a 3D printer. This is the SCA-1200HT Support Cleaning Apparatus.

main2.text: Some printed parts come out surrounded by soluble support material. This machine helps remove that support after printing.

choices.label: How does this machine remove it?

main3.text: The SCA uses a heated cleaning solution and circulation around the part. Compatible support material gradually dissolves away.

main4.text: This step is called post-processing because the printing itself is already finished. Now we're preparing the final part.

choices.label: Why not just pull the supports off?

main5.text: This is especially useful when support is inside cavities or around complex features that are difficult to reach by hand.

choices.label: What kinds of parts need that?

main6.text: So 3D printing doesn't always end when the printer stops. Cleaning can be an important final step in the workflow.

choices.label: Tell me about the cleaning process again.

main7.text: And that's station four! You've now seen printing, support material, and post-processing from start to finish.

choices.label: Take me back to the beginning.

what_is_sca.text: SCA stands for Support Cleaning Apparatus. Think of it as a finishing station for compatible 3D printed parts.

why_support.text: Supports act like temporary scaffolding during printing. They hold up features that couldn't print properly on their own.

choices.label: How does the SCA remove them?

temporary_support.text: Exactly. The support helps during printing but isn't meant to stay on the finished model.

choices.label: How do you get rid of it?

cleaning_process.text: The part goes into the cleaning system, where solution circulates around it. Compatible soluble supports dissolve over time.

part_stays.text: That's the idea. The process removes compatible soluble support while leaving the printed model you want to keep.

choices.label: Why not remove it by hand?

temperature.text: Temperature is part of the cleaning process. The SCA has different settings for compatible materials and cleaning conditions.

choices.label: Does every part use the same setting?

temperature2.text: Not necessarily. The correct cleaning conditions depend on the printed material, support material, and recommended process.

why_dissolve.text: Supports can surround delicate features or sit inside areas you can't easily reach. Dissolving them avoids pulling everything off by hand.

choices.label: So it's good for complex parts?

post_processing.text: Post-processing means work done after the printer finishes. That can include removing supports and preparing the completed part.

choices.label: So printing is only one step?

post_processing2.text: Exactly. Depending on the process, a printed object may still need cleaning or other finishing before it's ready.

complex_parts.text: Parts with internal spaces, overhangs, or hard-to-reach features can benefit from soluble support and automated cleaning.

cleaning_time.text: Cleaning time depends on the part, its geometry, support amount, and cleaning conditions. More complex parts may take longer.

materials.text: The SCA-1200HT is designed for compatible soluble-support workflows with materials such as ABS, PC, and nylon.

choices.label: Which printer here connects to it?

stratasys_connection.text: Remember the Stratasys printer at station three? Its soluble-support workflow is exactly why a cleaning system like this is useful.

tour_recap.text: You started with prototyping, explored materials and FDM, then finished here with support removal and post-processing.

question_menu.text: Of course! What do you want to know more about?

choices.label: How does this connect to station three?

tour_complete.text: You made it through all four stations! Thanks for checking out our 3D printing room.

bye.text: No problem! Feel free to keep looking around, and come back if you have more questions.
